newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Denmark sees lower German bond yield gap.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Denmark sees lower German bond yield gap.

text.p: Denmark's economy ministry said in its economic survey issued on Tuesday that it expected the 10-year bond yield gap between Denmark and Germany to be on average 50 basis points in 1998.
It expected the gap to be around 80 basis points in 1997.

At 0950 gmt on Tuesday the differential between the current benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 and the German bund was 53 basis points and the gap between the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark and the corresponding German paper 70 points.
The ministry survey also forecast that the 10-year Danish benchmark bond would yield on average 6.7 percent in 1997 and 6.6 percent in 1998.
Tuesday's yield on the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was around 6.45 percent with the seven percent 2007 bond at 6.59 percent.
The ministry said it based its forecast on estimates for both the current 2006 benchmark bond and its 2007 replacement due to become the sole benchmark later in the year.
